title: The lap with no return mark
body: The map's route ends at a chalk line. A keyring rests across the fold back toward the starting point; its tag has no place name.
rival_reading: A field crew could mark a temporary route and leave its gate key there; a missing place name does not prove an evacuation failed.
gloss: A route stops before its return and a key has no destination.

title: The bottle's ring crosses a row sketch
body: A clear ring dries across the notebook's crop-row drawing. The bottle cap is clean; the page beneath it is stained only where the drawn rows meet.
rival_reading: A response worker could record field conditions while checking a route; the ring and sketch do not establish that a program spread anything.
gloss: A water mark crosses a field sketch without showing its source.

title: Dispatch copy with an unfinished return
body: “Track access ends at the barrier. Keep the west lane clear for the last vehicle.” The receiving line is blank; on the back, someone asks for a green scarf to be saved.
rival_reading: A work crew could close its course and leave a receipt incomplete; the blank line does not show whether the order came from emergency response or a test.
gloss: A dispatch copy closes a route but records no receiver.

title: The row count continues past the page
body: The note lists three crop rows and a water check, then continues onto the cover. “Bring the small boots home” is written below the last line.
rival_reading: A responder could record conditions beside a closed route and leave a family reminder; the crop count does not prove a program malfunction.
gloss: A field count and a private reminder share one page.
